ADMISSION DIAGNOSIS:
James Foster, a 75-year-old man, was admitted with community-acquired pneumonia after several days of cough, feverishness, fatigue, and worsening breathlessness. The symptoms had reduced his ability to eat, drink, and manage usual activities at home. The admitting team considered the illness an acute lower respiratory infection acquired outside a health care facility. His history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and osteoarthritis was recorded as relevant background. He required inpatient care for respiratory support, antimicrobial treatment, and observation of his clinical response. The admission plan included reassessment of breathing, intake, mobility, and general tolerance of care. No other acute diagnosis was established during this admission. The patient and family were advised that the expected course depended on steady improvement in symptoms and ability to resume care safely at home.

REASON FOR ADMISSION:
Mr. Foster came to the hospital because his cough and breathing difficulty had progressed despite rest at home. He described low energy and reduced appetite, with less fluid intake than usual. His family noted that he was not keeping up with ordinary household activities and was becoming more limited by the illness. The combination of respiratory symptoms, age, and chronic conditions made home observation alone an unsuitable plan. The decision was made to admit him for treatment and monitoring, with attention to his breathing and ability to maintain oral intake. The suspected source was community acquired, and no recent institutional exposure was reported in the history available to the admitting team. He agreed with inpatient care and understood that discharge would depend on improvement and a safe plan for continued recovery.

His family encouraged evaluation when his breathing symptoms became more noticeable. The history was consistent with an acute respiratory illness, and the treating team diagnosed community-acquired pneumonia. No additional cause for the presentation was identified during the stay.
